source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Fluid status and diuretic needs can fluctuate, requiring dose adjustment based on ongoing clinical assessment rather than a fixed, unchanging dose","B":"Diuretic needs being considered essentially identical for every heart failure client, regardless of their individual fluid status","C":"Diuretics generally requiring fairly little ongoing monitoring once an initial starting dose has first been established","D":"Dose titration carrying fairly little established relationship to how well the client's symptoms are actually controlled"}}
source_row.rationale: Loop diuretic titration for heart failure clients requires individualized adjustment based on ongoing clinical assessment (daily weight, symptoms, physical exam), since fluid status and diuretic needs can fluctuate over time, rather than using a fixed, unchanging dose.
source_row.source_name: ACC/AHA/HFSA — Heart Failure Diuretic Management Guidelines
source_row.stem: A nurse titrates a loop diuretic dose for a client with heart failure based on daily weight and symptom monitoring. This individualized titration approach is used because:
